Definition: from G1569; to astonish utterly:--affright, greatly (sore) amaze.
BiblicalUsage: Scripture uses ekthambéō where we would say to be greatly amazed. In Mark 9:15, the text says "were greatly amazed." In Mark 14:33, the text says "and began to be sore amazed."
TheologicalSignificance: ekthambéō convinces me that miracles are not magic tricks; they are God showing His hand in the open. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: The Resurrection; The Healing of the Demon-Possessed Boy
